overall_evidence: The reconstruction includes many recognizable furnishings in a similar broad arrangement, but the view is much wider and more elevated, the prominent dark paneled door is not visible as such, and the flooring and table colors differ substantially. The reference's enclosed interior and large foreground furniture are presented at very different scales.

main_defects.evidence: The reference window, chairs and foreground desk occupy much more of the image; the reconstruction exposes the tops and outer sides of the room walls.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent size and placement differences may result from the viewpoint rather than object dimensions.

main_defects.evidence: The reference shows a broad dark door with eight rectangular panels, while the reconstruction shows no comparable door face or panels.
main_defects.uncertainty: The door may exist but be largely edge-on or occluded from this viewpoint.

main_defects.evidence: The visible floor and foreground work surfaces are much lighter and less textured in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and exposure may contribute to the brightness difference.

main_defects.evidence: The reference chairs show broad side profiles and gray shading; both reconstructed chairs read as upright, narrow white backs.
main_defects.uncertainty: The change in camera angle also affects the apparent orientation and silhouette.

main_defects.description: The blind appears smaller relative to the shelf and the overall wall in the reconstruction; the reference blind spans most of the shelf width and dominates the upper left wall.
main_defects.evidence: The reference blind is a major wall feature with a thick pale wood surround, while the reconstruction blind is smaller in the composition and its surround is much thinner.
main_defects.uncertainty: Perspective and camera framing influence apparent proportions.

strengths: The window blind is positioned above a low pale wood cubby shelf, with a slender floor lamp to the left and a white vertical unit to the right.
Two swivel chairs with wheeled bases and foreground work surfaces are present.
A spiky plant in a teal-colored pot is placed in the right foreground, as in the reference.
The room has pale walls and visible baseboards.
uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment, not human ground truth or a validated aggregate metric. Different camera placement and lighting complicate judgments of geometry, scale, orientation and materials. Objects outside the reconstruction view or seen edge-on cannot be confidently judged absent.
